house of beliefs and waiting for it to fall apart. It’s a very passive approach and frankly I
am not that patient to wait that long. But establishing that “observer” view point to stop
outside the house and then look at it and go: “Hey, what’s going on over here? Do i
really need this wall?” is very powerful and it’s one approach that we’re going to use.

2) The second approach we’re going to use is to start building another house, and start
creating a structure of beliefs, a whole new point of view, a whole different way of
expressing ourselves, that doesn’t involve the same victim or anger approach, where we
can create our own emotions, we can feel good and we don’t have to cry out for help to
protect us from emotional pain, because we create a realm of emotions, new belief
structure, that gives us immunity from emotional pain and feeling rejection. Then
building that other house is very much a part of that gratitude exercise i am about to
share.

3) The third approach to changing beliefs structure is to go into the house, your existing
core beliefs structure, and pull it apart. That is very powerful and it’s the fastest
approach I know, but it’s also the one that has most resistance and can be kind of
frightening. Going in and dissolving those walls, those characteristics of our
personalities, our habits, our behaviors, that we really believe are a way to protect
ourselves and to get help and to seek support, that often play out in a victim or an anger
role, is like collapsing the house while standing inside it – it’s kind of frightening. If we
take away all of our victim behaviors at once, now we feel really alone, no one to help us,
because that was the way that we sought help. How are we going to ask for help now? If
we take away all our anger approaches, how are we going to protect ourselves from
people that want to hurt us? How will we control others that may hurt us? How will we
push people away and protect ourselves?
Well, that’s not the only approach, but our mind is structured in a way that we need
these roles, emotions, need to play out these behaviors, even though we do not agree to
them intellectually or do not want them anymore, but down in a core belief system we
believe they provide a value to us and that we’ll have difficulty surviving without them,
because that’s what we learnt to believe years ago, that we need those behaviors in order
to survive or for our well being. Then going in and taking those out brings up a lot of
fear of being hurt, of loosing control, of what will happen to us and in order to avoid
that fear, another part of our mind goes in and keeps rebuilding the walls that we’re
trying to take down. That means we keep playing out those same habits of emotion that
we keep trying to dissolve.

Then in order to go about this very fast approach of going into those walls of habits we
play out, those structures of beliefs where we play out anger, sadness, victimhood, what
we want to do is first start by building another house and by house I mean a new
structure of attitude, emotion, belief, point of view and develop a whole different side of
our personality to live within, that will support an “observer” point of view, that we can
feel safe emotionally within and from that place of emotional safety we’ll allow

                                                                                                                                   2/6

ourselves to go look at our existing beliefs structure and start pulling it apart without
fear of the walls falling off, not having power, and therefore we won’t really need to rely
on those elements of anger, or victimhood or whatever else our habits of emotions
reactions and the core beliefs behind them are. We can safely pull them apart because
we live in the another set of beliefs or we start to live in another set of beliefs – that
second house. Then this first exercise of gratitude starts establishing the very
emotionally safe paradigm for us to take apart those core beliefs structures in a much
faster way, from emotionally safe vantage point. And it also builds an “observer” point
of view, that helps us step out of the reaction, the story, the momentum of emotion that
it’s often associated with.

This exercise helps us step out of that story and become an observer, which is something
that’s taught in all those spiritual traditions for a good reason. To understand it better
listen to an audio piece on “Emotional reactions”.

For this exercise you need to relax, close your eyes, put your attention on your breath,
and send gratitude to different aspects of yourself, your body and the world. As we learn
to direct our mind, we’ll learn that we can direct the thoughts we think, and if we can
direct the thoughts we think and the interpretations we make, we can start to direct the
emotions that we create and feel and start putting the power over our emotional state
back in our hands.

Guided Meditation:

What are you most grateful for? Today, in your life, in your past? Maybe it’s difficult for
you to see. Keep asking the questions and see where it could possibly go. Maybe it’s a
person, an experience. How does it make you feel?

Notice the feeling and breathe into the feeling that you have, and as you do that, let it
expand, become bigger and let your gratitude grow. And maybe you don’t feel the whole
lot of gratitude yet at this point, but as you practice, it can become bigger and more
noticeable. Then inhale to that gratitude and let it grow and expand, as if the oxygen
you were inhaling were the emotion of gratitude. And hold your mind to what you’re
most grateful for and feel the expression of gratitude go out to that what you are most
grateful for. As you breathe in oxygen, think of this as breathing in gratitude.
Gratitude’s filling your lungs, going into your heart like oxygen and is being pumped
throughout your body. Let the gratitude go through all your body, all the parts of it, all
the vessels and arteries, legs, arms, etc. Inhale gratitude, let it go through your body
and exhale it and feel it flow through your arms.

If you’re healthy, have arms and legs and other parts of your body, you have a gift
others don’t. Hugging others, making a meal, writing, feeding your self. Our arms and
hands are easily taken for granted. Just a simple act of brushing teeth for some people is
a challenge. The less you take all this for granted, the more gratitude you feel. Then
inhale into your whole body and the parts of it, for the ease with which all of them allow
you to live. And all your inner organs working together for you, the blood system, the

                                                                                                                                   3/6

skin, the bones, the strength. All of them – working the best they can. Send your
gratitude for working and doing what they do. Just for the simple action of digesting
food. This is a simple blessing not everybody has. Then you can choose to take it for
granted or you can choose to be grateful and send your gratitude. And if you’re listening
to this, you have ears that can hear. Not just my voice, but the voices of the people you
love, laughs, telephone, music, sound of wind through the trees, the sea, the bird
singing, the symphony. So much beauty can be perceived with your ears. Then send
your gratitude to your ears. You have the blessing not everybody has.

And if you have eyes and you can see, then you have the gift of sight that not everybody
has. Send your gratitude to your eyes, for all the different and beautiful things you can
see. Think of those different things you can see. And send your gratitude into your ears
again. If you can hear my words and you understand the meaning, then you have a
mastery over language and a healthy mind that can grow and allows you to function in
this world and take care of yourself – something not everybody is able to do. So send the
gratitude to your mind. Send it to your whole body again, to the different parts of it,
creating an expression, a living dream of gratitude inside that body, filled with emotion,
with a belief that you have many things to be grateful for.

Whether you feel the gratitude or not – keep considering the ideas. As you continue to
consider the ideas of what to be grateful for and how it benefits your life, that will
establish those ideas in your mind and will be building a whole new structure and a
whole new point of view to live from. One that is without anger, resentment, sadness,
victimization. Just by considering the ideas, the gratitude will come.

Go further. To expand your gratitude, inhale that gratitude into your lungs, into your
heart, into all the cells of your body, through the blood stream. And let it return back
into your arms. You’re breathing in gratitude like you breathe in oxygen and you exhale
gratitude as well. As you exhale gratitude, exhale it into the space around you, creating a
living dream of emotion. This is building a new house, a new dream of emotion to live
in.

And if you have a home, a roof over head, send your gratitude to that home. That’s more
than people have in the world. Electricity, heating, utility, air conditioning, send your
gratitude to all this. Whether your home is humble or huge, it protects you and provides
safety for you. Take a point of view of not taking it for granted. And be grateful for
having more than most people in the world. For the refrigerator. If you had a meal
today, send your gratitude you have something to eat. Food on the shelf.

This is more than many people have. This is not about feeling less for anybody else. But
this is about adopting a view point and see that we live in the world of abundance. If you
have a car or an access to public transportation and it can take you to whether you want
to go, than you have a means of travel that makes your life easier. And if you have a job
that provides you with income so that you can pay for your dwelling and food then send
your gratitude to your job, whether you enjoy it or not. It still provides you and makes
your life easier. A means of income is better than no means of income. If you’re the boss

                                                                                                                                   4/6

of the company then send your gratitude to your clients and to your employees that help
you take care of your clients and send your gratitude for how they help you with your
clients. Open up the channel of gratitude from you to them and open up that channel of
gratitude, thanking them, not with words, but with expression of emotion for bringing
the business to you. If you have a place of work. Add to your list – if you sit down and
have a meal, you can open a channel of gratitude and express it to the meal. If someone
cooked this meal for you, open a channel of gratitude and express it to them. Not with
words, but with emotion. A waiter or a waitress. A farmer, a track driver that brought
the food to the restaurant, the builder who built the place. All of them let you have the
meal. Then send your gratitude in all those different directions. With each inhale, inhale
gratitude and with each exhale gratitude to all this, to all the people that provide for
you.

This is something you can do throughout the day in various ways. Driving in a car, be
grateful for your car. Be grateful that someone built the roads that you can travel, that
there’re stop lights that keep you safe. All of this is making your life easy. If you are
stuck in traffic, you can complain, but it doesn’t make the traffic go away. You can’t
change the traffic, but you can change the story you tell and the emotions you express.
Then adopt one that is going to be more enjoyable instead of the one that creates more
chatter in your mind and more unhappiness. You can practice this exercise on a
meeting, in a subway, while eating the meal, while brushing your teeth or taking the
shower. You can express gratitude for having a healthy body, that you can wash
yourself, that you can brush your teeth. There’s no end to things that seem so ordinary
but won’t be possible without the benefit of the simplest things like hands, eyes, ears.

As you go throughout your day practice inhaling gratitude, sending it first through your
body and then exhaling gratitude and filling the room around you.

Do this practice periodically throughout the day. Maybe for 1 minute at a time, maybe
for 10 or 20 minutes at a time. Any action will be valuable practice.

Like I said there’s a number of reasons that I give you this exercise. It’s not a “wow”
kind of exercise, but it accumulates momentum and has a greater and greater impact
over time. One of the greatest impacts is that it’s starting to create a different house
than what we used to create that had emotional reactions. And from that new house of
beliefs, new point of view, it’s much easier to establish the whole “observer-witness”
frame. And that observer-witness frame is what will allow taking apart that other core
beliefs structure much more quickly. And taking apart that core beliefs structure is
something that we will begin to do in the next sessions. And if you have difficulty
creating the emotion, that’s okay. That’s where a lot of people start.

In order to support the process, get a book, a journal, and each day or as best as you can
throughout each day write what you’re most grateful for that day. And if you don’t even
feel any gratitude, still write what made your life easiest that day, what benefit did you
like the most that day. Whether you feel any emotion or not, beginning to write these


                                                                                                                                   5/6

thoughts will start to shift the way your mind thinks of things, and will start to affect the
way you process information, the way you interpret situations, and what you believe
about yourself and the world.

There’re faster ways to change beliefs and to become happy, but those other ways may
work faster if you practice this one.





                                                                                                                                   6/6

pages.text:
Pathway to Happiness

   pathwaytohappiness.com/courses/self-mastery-course-free/01-gratitude

                                                                                                       April 9, 2019




01 Gratitude

We’re moving all courses to the new Self Mastery Community




Watch Video At: https://youtu.be/CbNDLrEQDIw

Summary of practice

1. Listen to the Gratitude lesson audio. You may want to listen more than once.

2. Practice creating the emotions
During the day periodically create the feeling of gratitude and expressing it for what you
have in your life. It may be a few minutes at a time while you are on hold on the phone,
in the elevator, exercising, or commuting. It may be also be a longer focused
meditation.

3. Begin a journal and each day spend some time writing what you are
grateful for
This will help build and make your emotional practice stronger. If you are unable to
create the emotion of gratitude the writing will begin to re-wire the neural pathways in
your brain, and develop a different point of view so that you can work up to emotional
part later.

Some notes

This practice is a key ingredient to understanding and becoming familiar with how to
change your emotional state. Changes in your emotional state are accompanied with a
shift in your point of view and the dialogue in your mind. With this exercise you change
all three at once.

This exercise is something that you can practice as you go about your day or create a
specific meditation time. Do it for 3 seconds, 3 minutes, or 30 minutes at a time.
Whenever you think of it, create and share some gratitude for your breath, eyes, or
whatever else is in front of you.
                                                                                                                                   1/5

In order to reinforce the process I suggest you get a journal and each day write down
what you are most grateful for that day. You may find that in the beginning you are
writing about the same things. As you practice this exercise, the time you spend in this
point of view will grow. The more time you spend in the feeling of Gratitude, the more
you will see new things to be grateful for. The list in your journal then begins to grow.
Sometimes it takes practice to expand your perception.

You will get access to session 2 on Abdication of Power in 7 days. Use this time to
practice building new neural pathways in your brain with this exercise.

Resistance to change

There will be resistance, distractions, objections from your mind about doing this
exercise. That’s okay. We expect some resistance from the mind with each pattern we
work on changing. Working through resistance layers is just part of the work. If your
mind knew how to make the changes you wanted to make, they would have happened
already?

Your mind hasn’t been steering you towards what will make change. Typically your
mind will steer you back to the same starting point and the same beliefs they originated
from. A mind, by the time of adulthood, is just doing the repetition of what it already
knows. If you want change you need to do things it is unfamiliar with.

So what your mind wants as a process is something comfortable. It wants what it
already knows to do. This isn’t going to get you the changes you want.

Change is counter-intuitive to what the mind already knows. In learning to swim, one of
the things you learn first is how to hold your breath underwater. This is kind of the
opposite of swimming on the surface, but it is an important skill. You also learn to kick
your legs while holding the side of the pool. You also practice turning your head while
not going any where. These are all fundamental skills that you will put together later.
When you put them together you will be swimming. This is how the Self Master courses
are put together. You are learning individual skills, that when you put them together
will allow you to move through issues in your life with ease.

The other thing about swimming is that trying harder without good technique is just
flailing until you get tired. You are better off being relaxed in the water and developing
good skills.

Being practiced at gratitude is something that you might feel resistance to, but it will
give you skills in many areas. One important realization that you will need to reaffirm is
that you have power over your attention and therefore emotions. This awareness that
you can have power over your emotions will help build confidence that you can have
this power in other areas of your life.





                                                                                                                                   2/5

Use this exercise as a means to build confidence and faith in yourself that changes is
possible.

Change starts small. One step at a time. Then you practice taking many steps. After
many steps put together you will have completed your journey.

Common questions

What if I can't create the feeling of Gratitude
For some people it will be difficult to create or hold that feeling of gratitude. This is
particularly true if you have anxiety or depression. The longer you have had those two
issues, the more your adrenal system in your body is depleted and your glands are
unable to secrete the chemicals to change your emotional state.

If this is the case, no need to worry. Your process will just be a bit different. You will
need to eliminate some of the belief systems and internal dialog promoting the
depression and anxiety first. Lesson two on Abdication of Power will help with that
specifically. When those emotions are less strong, you will begin to feel more of the
good emotions.

If you have a lot of anxiety and depression, focus more on the journal writing part of the
exercise. You might not feel the emotions, but you can at least train your brain, and
build new neural pathways of what type of things to be looking for, and what to pay
attention to.

In this way you are working on the thought and perspective parts first, and the
emotional generation will follow later.

What if I get bored doing the Gratitude?
Some people find the Gratitude exercise to be uninteresting after a while. You might
even call it boring. You only have to survive it for a week before access to the next
exercise will show up. The Abdication of Power Session takes a completely different
approach to change. It uses a completely different part of your mind and will engage
you in a different way.

Being bored falls into the category of resistance. It’s the old part of your mind with your
old habits looking for a way to avoid this practice. A part of your mind is objecting to
feeling good feelings. In later lessons you will learn to identify that part of your mind as
a saboteur belief program. It would prefer that you have emotional drama instead of
some peace and gratitude.

Some part of your brain may want the excitement of anger, drama, fear, or the
dopamine rush of feeling like “you are smart” because you learned something new.
Notice these kinds of patterns of thoughts and how they try to steer your decisions into
old habits. For now just notice it and continue with the gratitude practice.



                                                                                                                                   3/5

This “just noticing” is a part of the awareness you are developing and will help you hunt
down resistance with other exercises. Hunting down these resistances and changing
them in each exercise will allow you to make changes faster.

So consider this as a challenge to change some of your old patterns.

How much time should I spend each day on this?
The amount of time that is right for you is different than for the next person. I am
hesitant to recommend an amount of time. For some people this will just be a standard
that their Inner Judge will beat on them for not achieving.

That said, 20 minutes is a good minimum to incorporate into your day. It might be a
solid 20 minutes or more in the morning or evening meditation. Or, you might fit in a
few minutes on your commute, as you prepare a meal, take a shower, and brush your
teeth. Three minutes during each of those things and you have made your 20

Each day is different. Some days might be hectic, and you forget altogether. The next
day you might have spontaneous gratitude about nice stuff in your life and it takes care
of itself.

How long will I be doing this practice?
The intent is that you will feel gratitude about things in your life everyday. So, for the
rest of your life. However, over time you won’t have to work at it. It will become default
way of looking at the world and appreciating your life.

In the beginning it may be somewhat like work because you are building neural
pathways in your brain and that takes effort.

Over the next few weeks, or months how much you emphasize this exercise the others
with your focus will be specific to your own personal change process. You might find
yourself avoiding this practice, or a different one for a few weeks, and then come back
to it later with a renewed understanding and appreciation for its value.

What if I have resistance to doing the exercises?
No surprise. Of course you are going to have resistance to the exercise. Your brain is
wired for habits, even bad ones, and to keep repeating them.

However, if you want change, you will do things that are new, unfamiliar, and
uncomfortable, or you won’t get change.

How uncomfortable is feeling gratitude compared to the old emotion or behavior your
want to change? Which would you prefer more? If you prefer the old habit of jealousy,
anger, insecurity, etc, then follow what the impulses of resistance and don’t do the work
to create gratitude. It’s your life. You choose the path and the results.

But this doesn't have anything to do with the issue I want to change?
Yes it does.


                                                                                                                                   4/5

Does the issue you want to change involve emotions?

Does the issue you want to change involve thoughts?

Does the issue you want to change involve what your mind fixates your attention on?

By practicing the feeling of gratitude you are developing the specific skills to direct your
attention, thoughts, and emotions in a way you want. If you can direct your attention
and emotions, then you can direct your behavior. These are fundamental skills you will
be building on to change any issue in your life.

How can I go faster?
It’s okay to sign up for the Self Mastery Basic sessions. You can do session 5 and beyond
at the same time you work on the free sessions of 1-4. They are all fundamental and can
be learned together. It’s okay to work on session 5 the same time you are working on
session 1 and 2 etc.

Supporting videos


Watch Video At: https://youtu.be/U9fdLhyPgLY

Approach this as training instead of gaining knowledge

The gap of several days between sessions is to give you time to practice. This is vital if
you are going to build new neural pathways. This is necessary so that you can create
different interpretations, change point of view, and change emotional responses.

Watch Video At: https://youtu.be/AHAgGXLGEVk

How to value your time

Awareness of your mortality can help you focus on what is important. With awareness
you don’t want to waste time, your attention, or emotions on suffering. You may have
to change your habits to make that happen.





                                                                                                                                   5/5

segments.text: This is Gary Van Wormer Dam, Pathway to Happiness.
And I'm going to talk to you a little bit about how to think about this Self Mastery Course
and the exercises and practices that you're going to get.
And one of the ways to think about it is training and practice.
And why it's set up the way it is, is you're going to have a gap between lessons.
Sessions are time gated, there's some days in between.
And that time is to allow you to practice the exercise, practice the skill, build a neural
pathway or begin to build a neural pathway that we'll continue and build on later and
expand on.
It's time to train your attention, to learn how to move emotions, to gather power that
you will then use for the next exercise or one or two exercises later will specifically
build on that.
So there are some fundamental skills you're building and they become more complex and
we build on those skills.
So one of the tendencies some people have, and you might notice this, is I want the next
session.
I want that information.
And part of that drive is in our mind we're driven by information because in school, for
the years of school, it was about knowledge.
You needed the information to pass the test.
You got the test.
You got the reward.
You've got that emotional satisfaction because you knew something.
Here it's about you're doing something.
In the beginning, any of these exercises might be uncomfortable.
If you already could master it, you wouldn't need to learn it.
But think about going to the gym.
If you want to train physically, you go to the gym and you get a personal trainer and you're like,
and you're like, okay, what are we going to do?
And it's okay, I want you to do this bench press
or go do a push-up.
And you do one push-up and he's like, okay, good,
you can stop, you know how to do that.
You've mastered knowing how to do a push-up or an exercise,
but you haven't mastered doing them, okay?
By doing them regularly, you can go up to five,
you can go up to then 10, and then you can go up to 30.
You can do a bunch more push-ups,
and then you can do them to where you don't get fatigued
when you do 30.
So then there's like, okay, I did 30 and then later on I can do another set.
Like, okay, now you have built neural pathways in your brain.
You've built muscle.
You've built power to do them.
You've also built a sense of confidence, a feeling in your body about doing it.
Same with these exercises because they're more skill-oriented.
They're like playing a musical instrument, writing a computer program, woodworking.
It's like something you practice.
Like, okay, I can do that.
If you go out and shoot basketball or golf and you, you know, it's like, oh, okay, well, I hit that one fine.
I guess I'm good.
I don't need to play anymore.
I don't need to practice anymore.
I don't think that would have gone over well with my coach who, you know, it's like, hey, coach, I made a free throw.
I don't need to shoot anymore.
It's like, okay, made one, but can you make one at the end of the game when you're tired?
Can you make one when all the fans are at the opponent's gym and they're screaming at you and it's unfamiliar surroundings?
Can you focus your attention then?
Can you calm your nervous system and your emotions so that you can focus and your muscles are shooting in the rhythm corresponding to your state instead of reacting to everything about you?
Can you calm and focus when that voice in your head is saying, no, don't screw it up, don't screw it up, don't screw it up, you know, which is getting you to imagine screwing it up, right?
So why do you practice shooting free throws? Why do you practice anything? So that you can do it under those conditions, okay?
So when a situation comes up and you start to have a reaction and it's hard to stop,
your practice is allowing you to calm yourself, shift your emotions, change your point of view and go,
have that sense of confidence, okay I got this.
So that doesn't come because you know, that becomes you practice and you know it intrinsically in your body and your nervous system.
and you have faith in yourself because you've done it fifty times, a hundred times, a thousand times.
So take the time in between these lessons to integrate into your nervous
systems, build the new neural pathways and they will also prepare you for future
sessions. If that helps, enjoy the practice. This is how you really get better.
